overview-s000.title: What You Will Learn in This Workshop
overview-s000.markdown:
This hands-on workshop is for FP&A / finance / corporate planning professionals who want to rethink Excel-centered budgeting, and for Power BI / Fabric implementation teams. It is designed for an in-person group of **10–20 customers in Japan**.

01 / Build a plan

Allocate company-wide targets and connect field input, locking, comments, and approvals.

02 / Compare assumptions

Use Optimizer, statistical forecasting, and scenarios to distinguish numbers that meet a target from operationally sound assumptions.

03 / Verify saved results

Learn to write back to Fabric SQL and verify saved values, not just success logs.

04 / Clarify implementation requirements

Review how actuals and plans are presented, permissions, capacity, and billing, then define success criteria to measure in your own PoC.
**Read about:** [Workshop objectives](#workshopの目的) / [Architecture](#アーキテクチャ) / [Getting started](#はじめ方) / [Lab list](#ラボ一覧) / [Deployment and AI prompts](#配備とaiエージェント向けプロンプト) / [Important notes](#開催と利用上の注意) / [Sources and license](#原典とライセンス) / [English summary](#english-summary)

overview-s001.title: Workshop Objectives
overview-s001.markdown:
Using the fictional Harborlight Provisions Co. as a case study, this workshop helps participants build an annual plan in Fabric Planning from data scattered across Excel and explain its assumptions and results. Designed for 10–20 customers in Japan evaluating adoption, it goes beyond a product demonstration to help participants define the business process, data, stakeholders, and PoC success criteria they should explore in their own organization.

By the end, participants should be able to: 1) allocate company-wide targets and connect input / review / approval; 2) explain the differences among actuals / plans / forecasts and how each is updated; 3) verify SQL writeback against both logs and actual data; and 4) review cost / capacity / permissions and define the scope of their own evaluation. Sample operations do not demonstrate performance, cost savings, accounting correctness, or production suitability.

overview-s002.title: Architecture
overview-s002.markdown:
1 / Import the source
Importing Northwind_FMCG.pbix creates both an existing report and a semantic model. Use the report to review existing performance; connect the Plan item to the semantic model.
2 / Required planning path
The main Plan connects to one semantic model and supports the sheets / Intelligence in Labs 01–06 and the capacity and governance review in Lab08. Do not change the connected model later, and do not rename it.

3 / Writeback and downstream analysis
Lab04 writes forecasts back to a separate Fabric SQL table. Standard SQL writeback does not automatically update the original semantic model or report. To use the data in a downstream model, explicitly configure the table addition / connection / refresh according to the official procedure.
4 / Optional Lab07
PowerTable is not a sheet in the main Plan; it uses a separate dedicated Plan and SQL database. It is an independent exercise that uses Microsoft's official asset-register XLSX as reference data.
**5 / Japanese-edition extension, Lab09:** Compare Gross Revenue / Forecast from Lab04 at the same Product × month granularity, copy them from temporary Lakehouse Files to a Warehouse, and verify the figures. Bind the Lakehouse managed Delta table, not the Warehouse, to Ontology / Graph; the Fabric Data Agent answers read-only questions through the Ontology. This does not write data back automatically to Plan / the source model. [Lab09](labs/09-variance-analyst.md) / [Synthetic sample CSV](data/lab09-variance-snapshot-sample.csv) / [Architecture diagram](assets/diagrams/lab09-variance-analyst.md) > **Verification status:** Parts 3–5 were exercised in Fabric using the included synthetic CSV; Warehouse verification, Lakehouse Delta, Ontology / Graph, and some Data Agent questions were checked. See [Lab09](labs/09-variance-analyst.md) for the scope of hands-on verification. **Referencing and copying are different.** A plan series referenced with From Sheets receives changes from its source. overview-s003.title: Lab List
overview-s003.markdown:
**The core path is Labs 00–06 and 08, totaling 165 minutes.** Adding optional PowerTable brings it to 195 minutes. Lab09 is an additional advanced exercise (45–60 minutes, excluding data preparation) and is not included in the core path or the 180-minute in-person workshop. Adding both Lab07 and Lab09 brings the estimate to 240–255 minutes. These are the sum of the time estimates for each lab, not a guarantee of completion including environment setup or wait times. overview-s004.title: Facilitation and Usage Notes
overview-s004.markdown:
**The default format is for the instructor to handle design / configuration while participants experience input / review / approval.** The [Facilitator Guide](docs/FACILITATOR-GUIDE.md) includes advance preparation, a 180-minute schedule, pair roles, recovery steps for common problems, and a PoC planning worksheet.
When product availability or screens differ from the materials The procedures and images include content checked in the author's Fabric environment in October–November 2026. Fabric UI and features change. **This does not assert that every individual feature, region, or tenant has the same availability.** Before the workshop, the instructor should rehearse in the actual account and environment and check the [official overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/iq/plan/overview), [prerequisites](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/iq/plan/overview-prerequisites), and [known limitations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/iq/plan/overview-limitations).
Choosing capacity and permissions for the group size Do not infer concurrent-use performance or cost from F2, the smallest capacity. Billing roles (Planner / Stakeholder / Viewer) are separate from workspace roles. Assign owners for capacity and costs. Use the activity-based estimates in the [Facilitator Guide](docs/FACILITATOR-GUIDE.md). Do not assume model RLS, input values, comments, and KPI visibility have identical scopes; refer to the limitations and verification steps in [Lab08](labs/08-sizing-and-governance.md).
Can the P&L model be used for production decisions? [Lab05](labs/05-pl-models-and-scenarios.md) distinguishes simple averages from quantity-weighted unit prices, annual from monthly values, and measures from row models. Do not treat the simplified exercise P&L model as a complete accounting model; separately verify your organization's definitions, aggregation granularity, signs for deductions, and expense scope.
